faq.q: Is my home warranty the same as homeowners insurance?
faq.a: No. Texas regulators distinguish a residential service contract from homeowners insurance. Identify the actual contract and covered event rather than relying on the word warranty.

faq.q: Does the plan prove an old appliance works?
faq.a: No. A plan document describes possible contractual benefits and conditions; it does not establish the appliance's present condition or guarantee a claim will be accepted.

faq.q: Will my existing plan automatically transfer to a buyer?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Ask the provider to identify any ownership-change requirements, costs, deadlines and remaining coverage in your actual agreement, then reconcile the response with the sale terms.

faq.q: Must I buy a warranty to sell to Cash As-Is?
faq.a: Do not assume a warranty purchase is part of a Cash As-Is proposal. Review the actual written agreement. Texas regulator guidance says a residential service contract is not generally required when purchasing a home.
